opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

deadlines.raw: 1st October 2026 (next bi-monthly deadline; deadlines on 1st Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, Dec)

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (up to £750 for Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Junior scientist members of the Genetics Society: Scheme A open to undergraduate, Master's and PhD student members and postdocs within 6 years of PhD viva; Schemes B & C open to PhD students and postdocs within 6 years of PhD viva (not undergrads/Masters). Applicants must present a poster or give a talk; supervisor must be a current member.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members at genetics conferences. Scheme A: attendance at Genetics Society/SIG meetings (travel & accommodation). Scheme B: attendance at non-Genetics Society meetings (travel, accommodation, registration). Scheme C: registration costs for virtual conferences.

opportunities.title: Training Grant

deadlines.raw: 15th November 2026 (quarterly deadlines at midnight on 15th Feb, May, Aug, Nov)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society, as long as studying or working in the UK or the course is held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisor must also be a member.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence, and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant

deadlines.raw: 1st November 2026 (quarterly deadlines at midnight on 1st Feb, May, Aug, Nov)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society, as long as studying or working in the UK or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisor must also be a member.
opportunities.summary: Funded by income from the journal Heredity; covers travel and accommodation costs associated with field-based genetic research projects that would typically produce results suitable for publication in Heredity.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any member of the Genetics Society with caring responsibilities, regardless of age of the person cared for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need.
opportunities.summary: Award to support attendance at Genetics Society meetings for members with caring responsibilities; funds can be used as the awardee thinks best supports their attendance.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting

amount.raw: Several sponsorship levels: a specific lecture for a few hundred pounds; a session up to about £1,000; major sponsorship of an entire meeting potentially several thousand pounds (major sponsorship over last 12 months between £1,000 and £2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Members of the Genetics Society. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK. Grants used towards organisation (not attendance) of a meeting.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society, usually one-off meetings with ad hoc organising committees. Several levels of sponsorship available.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant

deadlines.raw: 1st October 2026 (two deadlines per year: 1st March and 1st October)

opportunities.summary: Supports public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Funding covers eligible travel and materials costs (UK-based only).

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group (SIG) Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics research communities wishing to run regular series of meetings. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes for genetics research communities who wish to run regular series of meetings (Special Interest Groups).
